atomicity.reason: One obligation: open the contactors when any valid temperature reading is above 60 degC; the per-sensor sentence only fixes the scope of that single rule.

comprehensibility.reason: Intelligible on its own: trigger, threshold, scope and reaction are all stated in plain BMS vocabulary; the missing definition of 'valid' is scored under unambiguity.

feasibility.reason: A 60 degC per-sensor comparison on the 10 ms evaluation cycle is routine with thermistor/AFE readout, and it composes with the latch, reaction-time and record requirements without conflict.

parent_fit.reason: US_CELL_PROTECTION names 'rises above its safe temperature' as a disconnect trigger; the requirement supplies the limit (60 degC), the reaction (contactors commanded open) and per-sensor scope, matching the per-sensor intent recorded in RISK_THERMAL_RUNAWAY_PROPAGATION.

unambiguity.reason: 'Valid' is not defined for temperature: REQ_MEASUREMENT_PLAUSIBILITY and the acquisition element only classify cell voltage readings, so nothing says when a temperature reading is invalid; the body also widens from 'cell temperature' to 'every temperature sensor of the pack'.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define temperature-measurement validity (or extend the plausibility requirement to temperatures), or drop 'valid'; say 'every cell temperature sensor' if only cell sensors are meant.

verifiability.reason: Threshold, unit, strict comparison and per-sensor scope are explicit, so a bench test can drive one sensor just above and just below 60 degC and observe the contactor-open command (timing is bounded by REQ_FAULT_REACTION_TIME); the unclear 'valid' qualifier only narrows when opening is mandatory and is scored under unambiguity.

summary: Crisp, well-parented per-sensor 60 degC trip; its one gap is that 'valid temperature measurement' is not defined anywhere, because the plausibility requirement covers cell voltage only.
